newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian April-March coffee output off sharply.
newsitem.headline: Colombian April-March coffee output off sharply.

text.p: The chief of Colombia's National Coffee Growers' Federation said the country produced just 10 million 60-kg bags of coffee in April 1996 through March 1997, down from about 14 million bags in the same period 1995/96.
"There's a drop of nearly four million bags from one year to the other," federation leader Jorge Cardenas told reporters.

He declined to speculate on the impact of the drop on total production in the 1996/97 coffee year, but he said output between April and September was seen totalling not more than about 4.5 million 60-kg bags.

Cardenas, who spoke at an impromptu news conference after a weekly policy meeting, said the 4.5 million figure included expected production of three million 60-kg bags during the "mitaca" harvest beginning this month and ending in June.

He gave no reason for the sharp decline in production between April 1996 and last month, but heavy rain at the start of the year were widely seen as a factor that would cut into overall production figures.

In his remarks to reporters, Cardenas also said the federation had drawn since last October on about 1.5 million 60-kg bags of coffee in its inventories, leaving it with a current total of five million bags.
